title: Grateful Dead Live at Field House, Wesleyan University on 1970-05-03

ai_review.summary: A historically legendary Wesleyan show captured on a low‑fidelity audience mic – poor recording quality but an unforgettable anti‑war vibe.
ai_review.review: The tape is an amateur crowd‑mic capture that falls over, has frequent talk‑overs and a muddied mix, making it hard to hear the band.  Despite the technical flaws, attendees recall a magical evening of protest, acoustic set, NRPS backing and a surprise student composition from Jerry, giving the performance lasting cultural significance.

ai_rating.rationale: Almost all reviewers condemn the recording quality (≈2/5) while a few praise the concert’s historic atmosphere and specific moments, yielding an overall moderate rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crowd microphone frequently falls over, home‑brew mix with heavy talk, laughter and occasional clarity; music is often buried but some sections come through.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Concert began with an acoustic set (missing from this tape), followed by a New Riders of the Purple Sage segment, then the Dead.  The night was intertwined with anti‑war protests and spontaneous announcements, creating a relaxed, historic atmosphere.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His pedal steel work during the NRPS set was highlighted, and he played a student’s composition onstage.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron "Pigpen" McKernan's keyboards were praised as great.
